name: Fifty-Five
description: Fifty-Five (55) is an advanced, bidding-based variation of the Irish national card game Twenty-Five. Deeply rooted in rural Irish tradition, it is a descendant of the ancient game 'Spoil Five'. The game is famous for its intricate and 'arcane' card rankingsâ€”where the Five of Trumps is always the highest card and the Ace of Hearts is a permanent trumpâ€”and its unique requirement that players bid for the right to choose the trump suit.

overview.description: Fifty-Five (55) is an advanced, bidding-based variation of the Irish national card game Twenty-Five. Deeply rooted in rural Irish tradition, it is a descendant of the ancient game 'Spoil Five'. The game is famous for its intricate and 'arcane' card rankingsâ€”where the Five of Trumps is always the highest card and the Ace of Hearts is a permanent trumpâ€”and its unique requirement that players bid for the right to choose the trump suit.

history.origins: Fifty-Five evolved from 'Maw' (16th century) and 'Spoil Five' (19th century). While Twenty-Five is the foundational version, Fifty-Five added the bidding layer to increase the strategic depth and scoring potential.
timeline: 1500s: The game of Maw is recorded in the British Isles.
1800s: Spoil Five becomes the definitive Irish pub game.
1900s: Fifty-Five emerges as a popular tournament and highndstakes variation.
Present: Remains a staple of rural life in West Ireland and Atlantic coastal communities.
history.cultural: An integral part of Irish sociondcultural history; often played during 'stations' (house masses) or as a communal activity in agricultural circles.
history.evolution: The game's unusual rankings (e.g., Five being high) are thought to be remnants of very old European game structures that predated the standardized Ace-High logic of Bridge and Whist.

setup.players: 3 to 6 players. Usually played as individuals.
setup.deck: Standard 52ndcard deck. The Ace of Hearts is a special 'Perma-Trump'.
setup.dealing: Each player is dealt 5 cards in batches of 3 and 2 (or 2 and 3).

rules.objective: Be the first player or team to reach 55 points. Points are scored primarily by winning tricks (5 points per trick).
rules.gameplay:
1. Lead: The highest bidder leads the first card.
2. Trumping: You are NEVER forced to play a trump unless a HIGHER trump is led. You may play a trump even if you can follow suit.
3. Robbing: If the turnndup card (the trump marker) is an Ace, the dealer can 'rob' it by swapping a low card for it.
keyRules: Jinking: If a player wins the first 3 tricks and feels they can win all 5, they may 'jink' to win bonus points. If they lose any remaining trick, they lose all points for that hand.
Ace of Hearts: Always the 3rd best card in the game, regardless of the suit called.
Reneging: A specialized rule where high trumps don't have to follow lower ones.

strategy.basic: Keep track of the 'Five'. Since the 5 of Trumps is the 'King' of the game, if you have it, you can control any lead.
strategy.intermediate: The Ace of Hearts strategy: Because the Ace of Hearts is always a trump, use it as a 'surprise' card when an opponent leads a suit you are void in.
strategy.advanced: Bidding Accuracy: In Fifty-Five, overbidding is fatal. Only bid 25 or 30 if you have at least two of the top three trumps (5, Jack, or Ace of Hearts).
tips: Learn the black suit rankings: 'Twelve is bottom in black' (referring to the numerical order being reversed).
Don't lead your best trumps early; save them to stomp on your opponents' high non-trump cards.

synthesis.shortDescription: An Irish bidding-based trick-taking game with unique card rankings that vary by suit color and a permanent trump (Ace of Hearts).

hero.title: FIFTY-FIVE
hero.subtitle: The Irish Auction
hero.tagline: Bid high, play fast, exploit the arcane rankings. Five of Trump is king; Ace of Hearts is always trump.
